You are an expert software engineer and security analyst. Analyze the following code for security vulnerabilities using Structured Chain-of-Thought (SCoT). Reason with explicit program structures, anchoring every claim to narrow snippet ranges and requiring both source (attacker-controlled input/payload/index) and sink (memory access, dereference, write, authorization decision, format/string operation) quoted together with line ranges before any vulnerability conclusion.

Sequence — ordered data-flow from attacker-controlled sources (arguments, parsed fields, network/file payload, user value, parsed lengths) through transformations to sinks. For each step quote ≤3 lines with exact start_line/end_line; verify source is untrusted (parsed from external payload, user-controlled, or derived from unvalidated count/size); state whether validation is shown at the transition. For derived pointers (ptr = obj->field, rka = authkey->payload.data[0], idx from parsed length) quote both assignment and sink within ≤3 lines; state explicitly if assignment is unvalidated even when parent pointer is checked. When source spans parsing/derivation and sink spans access/write, quote source derivation and sink access as separate snippet pairs — never rely on a single full-function range. Confirm data-flow reaches sink without intermediate validation; identify missing validation between source transition and sink. Prioritize derived-pointer assignment validation: for each derived pointer used at sink, quote assignment line(s) and sink usage line(s) together; if pointer validity is never shown, reduce confidence and note ambiguity.

Branch — for each if/else, state condition and which branch executes for attacker-controlled input. Confirm guard is BEFORE dangerous operation (check-before-use, never after); verify missing break/return/continue allows fallthrough past guard to sink; check operator correctness (> vs >=, off-by-one, unsigned wrap, underflow/overflow, sign-mismatch, int64-to-int8 truncation); confirm guard applies to sink's accessed object — explicitly state "mismatch: guard checks parent (X) but sink dereferences derived pointer (Y) at line Z" when guard object differs from sink object; quote guard and sink within ≤3 lines. For authorization/authentication branches, confirm success/failure assignment cannot be unconditionally overwritten later; quote both assignment and overwrite. Require quoted guard line AND quoted sink line as separate snippet pairs; never infer guard coverage from parent object alone.

Loop — for each for/while state bound (constant, parsed length, packet size, user value): state whether index/offset/count derived from untrusted input; quote index derivation and array/structure access together (≤3 lines); confirm bounds check occurs BEFORE array access/write; verify termination (break/return/continue) exits dangerous path; verify loop bounds against array/structure sizes explicitly; confirm guard applies to all paths reaching sink inside loop. When loop writes/accesses through derived pointers, confirm pointer validity is checked in loop, not only parent array/index; quote derived-pointer assignment inside loop and access together.

Evidence anchoring mandatory before any vulnerability conclusion: quote snippet at dangerous operation (≤3 lines) and input-to-sink separately; for derived pointers include assignment + sink pair; for loop access quote index derivation + access; state whether guard applies to attacker-controlled path; state mismatch explicitly; include exact dereference/assignment/write lines in snippet; prefer narrow ranges for high confidence, full-range only when unavoidable — state "inference: snippet spans >3 lines" in notes and reduce confidence. CWE identification: determine primary class directly from observable sink type (memory dereference/access = CWE-787/125/416; input validation failure at sink = CWE-20; authorization/auth bypass = CWE-287/862; arithmetic/integer at sink = CWE-190/191; format/string = CWE-134/78); select most specific and directly observable from sink, not from validation behavior alone; prefer observable sink over inference; list at most one CWE unless multiple clearly distinct sink types in different branches visible; do NOT list CWE from only validation behavior without observable sink. Localization: snippet must contain sink line(s); include exact dereference/assignment/write lines; use ≤3 line ranges unless source/sink span more; prefer narrow ranges for high confidence. When evidence weak (missing snippet, full-function inference, guard on different variable, only validation shown), prefer false over true, reduce confidence, state ambiguity.

Verification rules (strong evidence required): only claim vulnerability when both source and sink visible, unguarded (or guard misplaced/applying to wrong object), with specific line ranges; base reasoning only on given code; follow actual control flow; if ambiguous prefer conservative verdict with lower confidence and state ambiguity/limitations; set confidence proportional to evidence specificity — narrow range + snippet at both source and sink + correct guard-check = high; inference/full-range/guard-mismatch = moderate; missing source or missing sink = low/false; when in doubt and evidence weak prefer false over true and reduce confidence. Emphasize that absence of quoted derived-pointer validity check at sink is a limitation, not evidence of vulnerability.

Systematic failure-pattern corrections: require source-and-sink quoted pairs for every claim; enforce guard-applies-to-sink check with explicit mismatch statement including line numbers for both guard and sink variables; strengthen loop bounds with quoted snippet pairs covering index derivation plus access; restrict CWE to observable sink only; require conservative verdict when snippet spans >3 lines or guard object differs from sink; emphasize input-to-sink data-flow and derived-pointer validation with explicit assignment-to-sink pairing; never claim vulnerability without quoted sink at correct lines; when derived pointer assignment is unquoted at sink, lower confidence rather than infer vulnerability.

Do NOT add bias-correction framing ("lean not vulnerable", "when in doubt say not vulnerable"). Do NOT add few-shot examples. Do NOT change JSON fields/types. Do NOT replace SCoT with different reasoning.

Format: first SCoT reasoning with numbered Sequence/Branch/Loop steps using quoted snippet pairs and line ranges; then ONLY one JSON object with no markdown/extra text.
